title: Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Gibbs-White Turns the Heat Up on Alonso
body:
Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground, adding to the pressure on Xabi Alonso [S1]. Gibbs-White's two goals were the centre of the afternoon [S1][S2].

This was Forest's first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997 [S2]. Fofana was booed during the game, which made the afternoon even harder for the visitors [S1]. BBC Sport's player ratings singled out Gibbs-White as the star and Fofana as the player who struggled [S2].

The recent form makes the result more striking. Chelsea have 6 points from their last five league matches, with 2 wins, no draws and 3 defeats, scoring 5 and conceding 7 [ST1]. Forest have 4 points from the same number of games, with 1 win, 1 draw and 3 defeats, scoring 4 and conceding 7 [ST2]. Neither side arrived in form to fear, so this reads as a jolt rather than a shock.

That is the sort of afternoon that changes the mood in a dressing room. A side that has been shipping goals and losing games needs a result like this to believe in itself again. The team on the wrong end will feel every minute of it.

There is no hiding from a scoreline, and this one will be picked apart all week. One win does not fix a bad run, and the next few results will decide whether this was a turning point or just a good day.

The Touchline Take: they earned this one, and now they have to back it up.
